text:
anya: Heads-up: thinking about consolidating our fallback signals into a lightweight collation service instead of lots of point-to-point webhooks. TL;DR: dedupe, apply per-tenant rate control, and emit a single canonical fallback decision. Thoughts?

mike: Love the idea. Main concern: adding an extra hop could increase decision latency. What SLO are we willing to accept for automatic fallback?

anya: Good call — goal is <=50ms on the fast-path for common cases. We can do sync fast-path + async reconciliation for noisy signals.

jorge: Fan-in is my worry. If every runtime instance sends signals for every anomalous request we get a storm. Need a compact signal shape + client-side sampling. Also per-tenant rate caps.

ellie: Suggest signal schema: {severity, origin, request_fingerprint, ttl, confidence, sample_count}. Fingerprint lets us dedupe across replicas.

mike: Sketch of minimal API: POST /v1/signals {tenant, fingerprint, severity, meta} -> 202 accepted + decision-id. Example payload:```json
{
  "tenant": "acme",
  "fingerprint": "fp:abc123",
  "severity": "high",
  "confidence": 0.86
}
```

anya: For dedupe we considered a sliding-window map keyed by fingerprint -> state({count, last_seen, aggregated_confidence}). Options: in-memory with TTL, Redis with eviction, or streaming aggregation. Tradeoffs: in-memory is fastest but loses data on restart; Redis centralizes but adds network hop.

jorge: Also cheaper to coalesce on client: local debounce + heuristic backoff on repeated signals for same fingerprint. But we still need server-side dedupe because multi-region rps.

anya: Agreed. For probabilistic dedupe we evaluated: Bloom filter (cheap but no deletion), Count-min sketch (good for counts), Cuckoo filter (supports deletes). Leaning toward small LRU cache + count-min for heavy hitters.

sre-bot: ALERT: last incident produced 8k fallback signals in 30s from tenant "test-org". CPU spike on collator pod at 78%. See logs:```text
[2026-03-18T12:01:02Z] recv signal tenant=test-org fp=xyz severity=high
[2026-03-18T12:01:02Z] aggregate fp=xyz count=1200
```

ellie: Security note: all signals must be HMAC-signed, and ingress must enforce per-tenant qps + burst. Also strip PII before collation.

mike: Operational boundary question: should the decision engine be colocated with runtime (local) or be a shared collator service?

anya: Tradeoffs: local decision = lowest latency and resilience (works if central collator down) but inconsistent global view. Central collator = consistent global decisions, easier to rate-limit and audit. Proposal: hybrid: local fast-path with conservative heuristics + central authoritative collator for cross-tenant/global decisions and reconciliation.

jorge: For local fast-path, runtime can hold small token bucket per-fingerprint and hit central collator async for escalation. If collator replies with "enforce", runtime applies immediate fallback.

ellie: Telemetry: emit counters (signals_received, signals_deduped, decisions_emitted), histograms for decision_latency, and sample traces for reconcilers. Tag metrics by tenant, region, and fingerprint-hash-prefix.

anya: Long-term refactor idea: unify this collator with rollout/orchestration service so rollouts can subscribe to the same signals. That lets A/B and canary flows share the same safety net. Event-sourced decisions give audit trail.

mike: Can we avoid a synchronous round-trip on the critical path? Maybe runtime applies local heuristic and only calls collator when aggregated confidence crosses threshold.

anya: Yes. Fast-path heuristic: if severity==critical and confidence>0.95 -> local immediate fallback + fire-and-forget notify collator. Otherwise local debounce + wait for collator decision within 50ms.

jorge: Implementation notes: collator endpoints should accept batched signals, support bulk ack, and provide backpressure headers (Retry-After / X-Collator-QPS). Use HTTP/2 or gRPC streaming for efficiency.

ellie: Also add an administrative API: GET /v1/decisions?tenant=...&since=... for auditors + web console. Export decisions to BigQuery for long-term analysis.

anya: Action items: 1) prototype in dev cluster: collator single-pod MVP with LRU+count-min, HMAC ingress, and metrics. 2) runtime change: local debounce + opt-in fast-path. 3) load test with synthetic signal storm. Who volunteers? :raised_hands:

mike: I can take the runtime debounce and fast-path hooks.

jorge: I'll own collator MVP + load tests.

ellie: I'll add the telemetry schema and security checklist.

anya: Thanks — I'll write a short RFC with API shapes and decision matrix by EOD tomorrow. :thumbsup:
